history.body: Hi, we have a young child and our rental is getting a bit tight. Is the 3-bedroom layout practical for a small family?

It could be a practical fit for a small family. Type A is 900 sq ft with 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms; the living, dining and kitchen are open-plan, and the layout avoids a long internal corridor and includes a small storage area. The third bedroom also gives you flexibility as your child grows. A viewing would help you judge whether the space feels comfortable for your family—would you like to arrange one?

That sounds more practical than where we are now. I’m still wondering if there’d be enough room for our child to play once we’ve got the usual furniture in. Do you have a floor plan I could look at first?

The approved Type A floor plan would be the best way to judge how much play space remains with your usual furniture. I don’t have the drawing to share in this chat, but I can check with the team for it. Exact furniture fit will depend on how you arrange the space.
Yes, please check and send it over if you can. Seeing the layout would help us picture where the play space might be. Thanks.
Thanks — I’ll share the approved Type A plan when it comes through. It should help you compare the living/dining area with your usual furniture and judge the potential play space more realistically.
